The ending feels entirely natural and purposeful, bringing the story’s central themes, imagery, and narrative structure to a cohesive conclusion. Throughout the piece, the writer carefully weaves together the imagery of the gutted, burned armchair and the rising floodwaters to reflect the silent, hollowed-out state of the couple's relationship (and the narrator's own quiet desperation). The climax occurs when the narrator explicitly connects Claire's "calcined blankness" to the ruined chair—realizing that while the outer structure of her life and marriage remains intact, the core has already been destroyed. When Claire closes the blinds with her "soot-stained fingers," it literally and figuratively ends the narrator's voyeuristic journey, leaving him alone in the rising water to confront his own isolation. Every detail builds toward this final, resonant image, providing a strong sense of thematic and emotional closure.
